The [[FIFA World Cup]] is an international [[association football]] competition established in [[1930 FIFA World Cup|1930]]. It is contested by the [[List of men's national association football teams|men's national teams]] of the members of the [[FIFA]], the sport's global governing body. The tournament has taken place organised every four years, except in 1942 and 1946, when the competition was cancelled due to [[World War II]]. A [[hat-trick]] occurs when a player scores three or more goals in a single match and it is considered an achievement, especially while playing at the largest international football tournament in the world. Across the over 1,000 matches at the 23 tournaments of the FIFA World Cup, 58 hat-tricks have been scored. The first hat-trick was scored by [[Bert Patenaude]] of the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]], playing against [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]] in 1930; the most recent was by [[Bukayo Saka]] of [[England national football team|England]], playing against [[France national football team|France]] on 18 July [[2026 FIFA World Cup|2026]]. The only World Cup not to have at least one hat-trick scored was the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] in Germany. The record number of hat-tricks in a single World Cup tournament is eight, during the [[1954 FIFA World Cup]] in Switzerland.

Only four players have scored more than one hat-trick at the FIFA World Cup: [[Sándor Kocsis]] (two in [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]]), [[Just Fontaine]] (two in [[1958 FIFA World Cup|1958]]), [[Gerd Müller]] (two in [[1970 FIFA World Cup|1970]]) and [[Gabriel Batistuta]] ([[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994]] and [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]]) — the latter being the only player in history to score hat-tricks at two World Cups. 20 players have scored a hat-trick in the knockout stage of the FIFA World Cup. Two were playing in their first ever World Cup match, [[Edmund Conen]] and [[Angelo Schiavio]], both in [[1934 FIFA World Cup|1934]], a tournament without a group stage. [[Geoff Hurst]] (1966) and [[Kylian Mbappé]] (2022), who also scored 2 penalties, are the only players to have scored a hat-trick in [[List of FIFA World Cup finals|the final]]. Two players have scored a hat-trick in the second group stage of the World Cup, [[Paolo Rossi]] and [[Zbigniew Boniek]], both in [[1982 FIFA World Cup|1982]].

==Notable World Cup hat-tricks==
{{hatnote|This section features records and notable hat-tricks relating to the men's World Cup. For notable hat-tricks at the Women's World Cup, see [[List of FIFA Women's World Cup hat-tricks#Notable World Cup hat-tricks]].}}

*[[Bert Patenaude]] was the '''first player to score a hat-trick''' in a World Cup match, on 17 July 1930 against [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]]. However, until 10 November 2006 the first hat-trick that FIFA acknowledged had been scored by [[Guillermo Stábile]] of [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]], two days after Patenaude. In 2006, FIFA announced that Patenaude's claim to being the first hat-trick scorer was valid, as teammate [[Tom Florie]]'s goal in the match against Paraguay was re-attributed to him.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fifa.com/world-match-centre/news/newsid/107/499/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140415092621/http://www.fifa.com/world-match-centre/news/newsid/107/499/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 15, 2014 |title=American Bert Patenaude credited with first hat trick in FIFA World Cup history |date=19 November 2006 |access-date=23 June 2014 |publisher=FIFA Official Website}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fifa.com/fifaplus/en/articles/bert-patenaude-and-world-cups-first-ever-hat-trick |title=Bert Patenaude and World Cup's first-ever hat-trick |date=1 May 2023 |access-date=13 March 2024 |publisher=FIFA Official Website |archive-date=13 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240313081900/https://www.fifa.com/fifaplus/en/articles/bert-patenaude-and-world-cups-first-ever-hat-trick |url-status=live }}</ref>
*Four players have scored '''two hat-tricks''' in World Cup matches: [[Sándor Kocsis]] (both [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]]); [[Just Fontaine]] (both [[1958 FIFA World Cup|1958]]); [[Gerd Müller]] (both [[1970 FIFA World Cup|1970]]); and [[Gabriel Batistuta]] ([[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994]] and [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]]).<ref name="HeroicHT">{{cite news |url=https://www.fifa.com/newscentre/features/news/newsid=1409096/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140709174545/http://www.fifa.com/newscentre/features/news/newsid=1409096/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 9, 2014 |title=A handful of heroic hat-tricks |date=2 April 2011 |access-date=23 June 2014 |publisher=FIFA Official Website}}</ref> Batistuta is thus the only person to score hat-tricks in two World Cups. He has another unique record of scoring hat-tricks, both were achieved on 21 June of the year, against World Cup finals debutants (Greece and Jamaica), and each time the third goal was a penalty.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20081203015017/http://www.fifa.com/mm/document/fifafacts/mcwc/ip-301_02a_fwc_goals_22689.pdf FIFA.com]</ref> Kocsis and Müller scored their hat-tricks in consecutive matches.
*[[Oleg Salenko]] is the only player in World Cup history to have '''scored five goals in a single match'''. He did this during the [[1994 FIFA World Cup]] match between [[Russia national football team|Russia]] and [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/26252836 |title=World Cup moments: Five for Salenko |date=30 April 2014 |access-date=23 June 2014 |publisher=BBC |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140430141948/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/26252836 |archive-date=30 April 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*One player has scored a '''hat-trick on his international début''': [[Guillermo Stábile]] ([[1930 FIFA World Cup|1930]]).<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/18529/6132521/guillermo-stabile |title=Guillermo Stabile |date=14 May 2010 |access-date=23 June 2014 |publisher=[[Sky Sports]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305065401/http://www.skysports.com/football/news/18529/6132521/guillermo-stabile |archive-date=5 March 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*One player has scored '''four goals for the losing side''': [[Ernst Wilimowski]] (5–6, [[1938 FIFA World Cup|1938]]).<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/38-best-wc-game-you-never-saw |title=The best World Cup game you never saw |date=8 June 2010 |access-date=23 June 2014 |publisher=[[Four Four Two]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924015352/http://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/38-best-wc-game-you-never-saw |archive-date=24 September 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*Two players have scored a '''hat-trick for the losing side''': [[Josef Hügi]] (5–7, [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]]) and [[Igor Belanov]] (3–4, [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986]]).
*Two other players have scored a '''hat-trick in a game that their side did not win''': [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] (3–3, [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]])<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/jun/15/spain-portugal-world-cup-group-b-match-report|title=Cristiano Ronaldo hits hat-trick as Portugal deny Spain in six-goal thriller|first1=Sid|last1=Lowe|work=The Guardian |date=June 15, 2018|via=www.theguardian.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615224845/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/jun/15/spain-portugal-world-cup-group-b-match-report|archive-date=June 15, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> and [[Kylian Mbappé]] (3–3, losing 4–2 on penalties, [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]]).
*There have been three occasions when '''two hat-tricks have been scored in the same match'''. Two occurred during the [[1938 FIFA World Cup]]: when [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]] defeated [[Cuba national football team|Cuba]], [[Gustav Wetterström]] and [[Harry Andersson]], both playing for Sweden, scored three goals, with the former completing his in the first half. In the [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] vs [[Poland national football team|Poland]], [[Leônidas (footballer, born 1913)|Leônidas]] did it for Brazil and [[Ernst Wilimowski]] for Poland. One occurred in [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]]: when [[Austria national football team|Austria]] defeated [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]], [[Theodor Wagner (footballer)|Theodor Wagner]] and [[Josef Hügi]] scored hat-tricks for Austria and Switzerland respectively.
*Two players have scored '''hat-tricks in World Cup Finals'''. [[Geoff Hurst]] scored three goals for [[England national football team|England]] against [[Germany national football team|West Germany]] in the [[1966 FIFA World Cup final|1966 final]].<ref name="HeroicHT"/><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.thefa.com/England/All-Teams/Players/H/Geoff-Hurst |title=Geoff Hurst Biography |access-date=23 June 2014 |publisher=[[The Football Association]] Official Website |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101127001035/http://www.thefa.com/England/All-Teams/Players/H/Geoff-Hurst |archive-date=27 November 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> This is also the '''longest hat-trick''' to be completed — most time between the first and third goals. His first goal came at 18', while the second and third goals were in [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]] at 98' and 120'. [[Kylian Mbappé]] scored the other World Cup finals' hat-trick in the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] [[2022 FIFA World Cup final|final]] for [[France national football team|France]] against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]]. His goals were scored at the 80th, 81st and 118th minute marks. Two of his goals - 80th and 118th - were successful penalty kicks. 
*The '''quickest hat-trick''' by a player is [[Erich Probst]], who scored at 4', 21', and 24' in [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]], playing for [[Austria national football team|Austria]] against [[Czechoslovakia national football team|Czechoslovakia]] in the first round.  
*The '''briefest hat-trick''' to be completed — that is, the shortest time between the first and third goals — is the one by [[László Kiss (footballer)|László Kiss]] in [[1982 FIFA World Cup|1982]] against [[El Salvador national football team|El Salvador]]. He scored at 69', 72', and 76', making the time between his first and third 7 minutes. This is also the '''only hat-trick scored by a substitute'''.
* The only players to have '''scored from three headers''' in a single match are [[Tomáš Skuhravý]] in [[1990 FIFA World Cup|1990]] and [[Miroslav Klose]] in [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002]].<ref name="HeroicHT"/>
*The '''youngest player''' to score a hat-trick is [[Pelé]], at 17 years, 244 days ([[1958 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Brazil vs France|5–2]] against [[France national football team|France]] in [[1958 FIFA World Cup|1958]]).
*The '''oldest player''' to score a hat-trick is [[Lionel Messi]], at 38 years, 357 days ([[2026 FIFA World Cup Group J#Argentina vs Algeria|3–0]] against [[Algeria national football team|Algeria]] in [[2026 FIFA World Cup|2026]]).<ref name=":0" />
*Germany (incl. West Germany) holds the record for '''most hat-tricks scored''' with 7. Germany also shares with South Korea the record for '''most hat-tricks conceded''' with 4.
